title: The People's Republic of China Third National Communication on Climate Change
organization: People's Republic of China; submitted to the UNFCCC
temporal_coverage: Government-approved communication dated December 2018; observed climate and sector trends and future scenarios, generally updated through 2015.
methodology: Government-approved UNFCCC report combining observed trends and modeled risks.
limitations: Unofficial translation; underlying studies are dated and projections are not measurements.

title: Progress Report on China's Climate Change Adaptation (2024) / 中国适应气候变化进展报告（2024）
organization: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China
temporal_coverage: Official 33-page review of climate conditions and adaptation activities in 2024; includes implementation status through February 2025.
methodology: Ministry report reviewing national climate observations, sector actions and regional adaptation measures.
limitations: Government progress account; program coverage and reported outputs are not independent outcome evaluations.

title: 2024 national situation of natural disasters
organization: National Commission for Disaster Prevention, Reduction and Relief Office and Ministry of Emergency Management of China
temporal_coverage: Calendar-year 2024 disaster impacts reported by local emergency-management departments and reviewed by national agencies.
methodology: Annual bulletin compiled from local emergency reports and inter-agency review; includes hazard-specific and regional totals.
limitations: Administrative impact estimates; the bulletin does not attribute individual disasters to climate change.

title: MEM publishes typical cases of successful disaster avoidance in 2024 / 应急管理部公布2024年度全国成功避险避灾典型案例
organization: Ministry of Emergency Management of China
temporal_coverage: National ministry's selected 2024 disaster-avoidance cases, published 6 June 2025.
methodology: Ministry-selected case reports drawn from local submissions and expert review of 437 reported cases.
limitations: Selected successful cases illustrate response processes, not representative rates or independently evaluated impact.
